cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll run the cupboard clear-out. Help me sort these committee folders?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure. What are we throwing away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing yet. These unpaid bills are why I want a new treasurer. Put them in meeting order.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I came to tidy, not accuse someone in front of everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll ask the questions. Sit beside me and find each bill when I need it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads a clear-out and recruits help; A3 changes it to replacing the treasurer; A5 takes the public role to keep B recruited behind the new goal.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 disposal question prompts A3 preservation of unpaid bills; B4 accusation objection causes A5 division of speaking and document support.

relationship.evidence: B2 expects a simple task and B4 resists a public confrontation, a credible change once the truth is revealed.

heightening.evidence: A5 recruits B again to the now-explicit challenge through a role that addresses B4 fear.

specificity.evidence: A1 committee folders and A3 unpaid bills supply why tidying becomes opposition.
